It is not for those looking exclusively for entertainment but instead the heady play of ideas.
As theatre, Baldwin and Buckley at Cambridge may lack urgency, but the impossible task of creating an equitable and accepting society remains as crucial as ever.
Buckley and Baldwin at Cambridge has other weaknesses.
Better to recall that the memorable Cambridge debate also happened and is importantly remembered here in only slightly compromised form.
Elevator Repair Service may be conducting an experiment pitting style against substance, in which case the former distressingly wins.

Alas, after Stevenson stops speaking, Sargeant and Williams walk on stage to begin the real debate — very traditional casting here — and the “Baldwin & Buckley at Cambridge” falls back to earth with a thud.
If your goal is to savor Baldwin’s response, mull it over, plumb its depths, you may need to resort to the historical record or better yet YouTube, where the exchange is preserved for posterity.
Elevator Repair Service is a master of theater of the essence of America.
The hourlong production by the Elevator Repair Service is a riveting mixture of naturalism with occasional touches of theatricality and experimentation.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this verbatim recreation of the 1965 Baldwin-Buckley debate, with some finding it mesmerizing and timely while others question why the theatrical staging adds value over simply watching the YouTube video.
